extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in commutative algebra / algebraic number theory
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, equivalences, and structural criteria for Noetherian rings: Serre conditions (Rn),(Sn), normality, Dedekind domains, fractional ideals/invertibility, and valuation rings; used to determine when rings have these properties and to compute ideal-theoretic invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre's Condition (R n)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Rn) holds if, for any prime p of height m ≤ n, the localization R_p is regular of dimension m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'We say Serre’s Condition (Rn) holds if, for any prime p of height m ≤ n, the localization R_p is regular of dimension m.' (Used to test local regularity up to height n; special cases discussed: (R0), (R1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre's Condition (S n)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Sn) holds if, for any prime p of any height m, the depth of p on R_p is at least min{m,n}, equivalently depth(R_p) ≥ min{ dim(R_p), n }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording and equivalence given: 'We say Serre’s Condition (Sn) holds if ... depth(R_p) ≥ min{ m, n }, or equivalently, if depth(R_p) ≥ min{ dim(R_p), n }.' Note: (Sn) is equivalent to R_p being Cohen–Macaulay when depth(R_p) < n; special case (S1) means there are no embedded primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: (R0) characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: (R0) holds iff R_p is a field for any minimal prime p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: '(R0) holds if and only if R_p is a field for any minimal prime p.' Use to check behavior at minimal primes (reducedness interplay with (S1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: (R1) characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: (R1) holds iff (R0) holds and R_p is a DVR for any prime p of height 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: '(R1) holds if and only if (R0) does and R_p is a DVR for any p of height-1.' Useful for detecting normality in codimension 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: (S1) consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: (S1) holds iff each associated prime p in Ass(R) is minimal, i.e., there are no embedded primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original reasoning: 'In particular, (S1) holds if and only if p is minimal when p ∈ Ass(R) ... that is, there are no embedded primes.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced iff (R0) and (S1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Noetherian ring R is reduced if and only if (R0) and (S1) hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Exercise (23.15): use this as a test for reducedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Height-1 primes vs depth-1 primes (Lemma 23.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Σ = {p prime | ht(p)=1} and Λ = {p prime | depth(R_p)=1}. Then Σ ⊆ Λ, and Σ = Λ iff (S2) holds. Also R = ⋂_{p ∈ Λ} R_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original lemma states these containments and equivalence; it gives a way to reconstruct R as an intersection of localizations at primes of depth 1 and links (S2) to equality of the two sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection description for normal Noetherian domains (Theorem 23.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a normal Noetherian domain then R = ⋂_{p prime, ht(p)=1} R_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses normality to deduce depth(R_p)=1 iff dim(R_p)=1; hence intersection over height-1 primes recovers R. Useful as a criterion/characterization of normal domains in dimension ≥1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre's Criterion for Normality (Theorem 23.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Noetherian domain R is normal if and only if (R1) and (S2) hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: 'R is normal iff (R1) and (S2) hold.' Proof given by checking integrality locally and using Lemma (23.16). This is the standard Serre criterion for normality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normality criterion for plane curves (Example 23.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: For R = k[X,Y]/⟨f⟩ with k algebraically closed and f irreducible (plane curve), R is normal ⇔ the partials ∂f/∂X and ∂f/∂Y do not both belong to any maximal ideal containing f; equivalently the curve f=0 is nonsingular everywhere or ⟨f, f_X, f_Y⟩ = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a geometric algebraic criterion for normality (nonsingularity) of plane curves; used as an explicit test in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Dedekind domain (24.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A domain R is Dedekind if it is Noetherian, normal, and of dimension 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original definition: 'Dedekind domains are defined as the normal Noetherian domains of dimension 1.' This is the central definition used for the remainder of the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local characterization of Dedekind domains (24.7 / 24.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Noetherian domain R (not a field) is Dedekind iff R_p is a DVR for every nonzero prime p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition (24.7) and related exercises: tests Dedekind property by checking local DVR condition at nonzero primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main Theorem of Classical Ideal Theory (24.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Dedekind domain R every nonzero ideal a factors uniquely as a product of prime ideals: a = ∏_p p^{v_p(a)}, where v_p are valuations from the DVR localizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives existence and uniqueness of prime factorization of ideals in Dedekind domains; includes formula and explanation using local valuations v_p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary ideals in dim 1 Noetherian domains (24.9 and Corollary 24.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Noetherian domain of dimension 1 every nonzero ideal has a unique primary decomposition with primary components q_i whose primes p_i are distinct; furthermore, R is Dedekind iff every primary ideal is a power of its radical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition (24.9) proves uniqueness of primary decomposition in dim 1; Corollary (24.11) gives a useful criterion for Dedekind: each primary ideal equal to a power of its radical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness of integral closure under separable extensions (Theorem 24.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be a normal Noetherian domain with fraction field K, and let L/K be a finite separable field extension. Then the integral closure R' of R in L is module-finite over R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses trace pairing and Galois closure. Remark: separability is necessary for module-finiteness in general (Akizuki counterexamples when inseparable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral closure of Dedekind domains in finite separable extensions (24.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is Dedekind and L/K is a finite separable extension then the integral closure R' of R in L is Dedekind (Noetherian, normal, dim 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary of (24.17): module-finiteness preserves Noetherian property, normality, and dimension; used to show rings of integers are Dedekind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noether's Theorem for finite extensions over char 0 (24.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k be a field of characteristic 0 and R a finitely generated k-algebra domain. For any finite field extension L of Frac(R), the integral closure R' of R in L is a finitely generated R-module and a finitely generated k-algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Noether normalization and separability (characteristic 0 guarantees separability); gives practical criterion for finiteness of normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of fractional ideal and operations (25.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fractional ideal M of a domain R with fraction field K is an R-submodule of K. Product M N := {∑ x_i y_i | x_i∈M, y_i∈N}. Quotient (M : N) := { z ∈ K | zN ⊆ M }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic definitions used to talk about invertibility, principal fractional ideals, and ideal arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness conditions for fractional ideals (Proposition 25.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a fractional ideal M the following are considered: (1) M = (a : b) for integral ideals a,b with b≠0; (2) exists x ∈ K^× with xM ⊆ R; (3) exists nonzero x ∈ R with xM ⊆ R; (4) M finitely generated. (1),(2),(3) are equivalent; they are implied by (4); all four are equivalent for every M iff R is Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives practical equivalent criteria to detect fractional ideals that are 'integral-type' and links to Noetherian property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization compatibility for fractional ideal operations (Lemma 25.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a multiplicative set S, S^{-1}(M N) = (S^{-1}M)(S^{-1}N) and S^{-1}(M : N) ⊆ (S^{-1}M : S^{-1}N), with equality if N is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful localization rules when checking local principality or invertibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally principal fractional ideal (Definition 25.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fractional ideal M is locally principal if for every maximal ideal m the localization M_m is principal over R_m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This local condition is central to invertibility tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invertible fractional ideal (Definition and Prop 25.7–25.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fractional ideal M is invertible if there exists M^{-1} with M M^{-1} = R. If M is invertible then M^{-1} = (R : M), and M is finitely generated and nonzero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invertibility gives uniqueness of inverse and implies finiteness; provides method to compute inverse as (R:M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invertible in local domain ⇔ principal (Lemma 25.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a local domain, a fractional ideal M is invertible iff M is principal and nonzero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local test: invertibility reduces to principality in local rings (used in proofs of global criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Global characterization of invertibility (Theorem 25.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fractional ideal M is invertible iff M is finitely generated and locally principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a practical global criterion: check finite generation and principality at all maximal ideals (or localizations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invertibility and valuations in Dedekind domains (Theorem 25.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Dedekind domain R, for a,b nonzero integral ideals M := (a : b) is invertible and factors uniquely as M = ∏_p p^{v_p(M)}, where v_p(M) := min{v_p(x) | x ∈ M}; if x_i generate M then v_p(M) = min_i v_p(x_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives computational formula for valuations of fractional ideals and their unique prime-power factorization in Dedekind domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterizations of Dedekind via ideals and modules (Theorem 25.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a domain R the following are equivalent: (1) R is Dedekind; (2) every integral ideal is invertible; (3) every integral ideal is projective; (4) every integral ideal is finitely generated and flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides multiple algebraic/ module-theoretic tests for Dedekind property; useful for proving equivalences in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian domain Dedekind characterization via torsion-free modules (Theorem 25.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Noetherian domain R is Dedekind ⇔ every torsion-free module is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a module-theoretic global criterion: test flatness of torsion-free modules to detect Dedekind property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picard group / Ideal class group identification (25.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring R, Pic(R) = isomorphism classes of invertible modules (group under tensor); for a domain R invertible fractional ideals form F(R), principal ideals P(R) form kernel of map F(R) → Pic(R). The ideal class group F(R)/P(R) ≅ Pic(R). Pic(R)=0 iff R is a UFD/PID (in Dedekind case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the connection between modules and ideal-theory: Picard group measures failure of principality; invertible module tests (Exercise 25.17) give equivalent characterizations: invertible ⇔ finitely generated and locally free rank 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation ring definition (26.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A subring V of a field K is a valuation ring of K if whenever z ∈ K^×, either z ∈ V or 1/z ∈ V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent formulations: ideals totally ordered by inclusion; V is a local normal domain maximal under domination. Provides base definition for valuation-theoretic tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal ideal and locality of valuation rings (Prop 26.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For valuation ring V of K the set m := {1/z | z ∈ K^×  ackslash V} ∪ {0} is the maximal ideal; V is local and K is its fraction field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives explicit description of the maximal ideal in a valuation ring; used in dominance and domination arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation rings dominate local subrings (Prop 26.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a field K and a local subring A, A is dominated by a valuation ring V of K (i.e., V ⊇ A and V's maximal ideal contracts to A's maximal ideal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructed by Zorn's lemma; ensures existence of valuation overrings dominating a given local ring (useful for testing integral closure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral closure equals intersection of valuation overrings (Theorem 26.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The integral closure R' of a subring R ⊆ K is the intersection of all valuation rings V of K containing R. If R is local, the valuation rings dominating R suffice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a criterion to test integrality: to check x ∈ R' check membership in every valuation overring containing R; used to characterize normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuations and value-group properties (26.12–26.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: A valuation v: K^× → Γ (totally ordered additive group) satisfies v(xy)=v(x)+v(y) and v(x+y) ≥ min{v(x),v(y)} (with equality when v(x)≠v(y)). The valuation ring is {x | v(x) ≥ 0}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the algebraic axioms that translate valuation rings into ordered-group valued maps; examples include DVR (Γ ≅ Z) and group-algebra constructions; propositions give consequences for sums and linear relations among elements.
